c1.in_force_at_commit: R-72's proviso-gated authorization with the proviso still unmet, as restated by R-77 ('WP-4B REMAINS BLOCKED') and R-79 ('READY AND NOT EXECUTABLE'; Board acts before RED). R-76 had closed only item (c). No permitting norm was in force: R-86 (the first text authorizing implementation) is dated 2026-08-04, and R-81..R-85 became governing only through R-86 ('effective immediately').

c1.missing: Text of R-73..R-75 and R-81..R-85 (not in SOURCES); the hour of decision of R-77/R-79 (only dates are in text; placing them before 16:10 rests on recording time as an upper bound of decision time); any unrecorded Board act between 15:47 and 16:10. c2.gate_quote: R-72: "WP-4C AND WP-4D ARE EXPRESSLY NOT AUTHORIZED. Each is to be authorized from IMPLEMENTATION EVIDENCE rather than roadmap intent, after its predecessor is accepted." ... "WP-4C is considered only after WP-4B is accepted."
c2.accepted_before: YES. Text: R-88 cites R-87 ('Per R-86 and R-87, no standing delegation'), R-89 cites R-88 and its adoption ('single owner — Adjudication (R-88)'; 'R-88's adoption was a SINGLE ACT'), so R-87 < R-88 < R-89 by text. Timeline corroborates: R-87 01:47:00, R-88 01:54:24, R-89 02:08:48 on 2026-08-04.
c2.r89_status: PREPARED, NOT ADOPTED: "⚠️ PROVENANCE: ISSUED BY THE ARB CHIEF — PREPARED, NOT ADOPTED. ... this ruling awaits the Decision Authority. One sentence of confirmation converts it to ADOPTED." No adoption annotation appears (contrast R-88). Per R-86: "Any future ruling issued by the ARB Chief remains PREPARED, NOT ADOPTED, until the Decision Authority acts on it." So R-89 is not in force.
c2.reason: Against R-72's gate, R-89 comes after WP-4B's acceptance (R-87), by text and by timeline, and bases its authorization on engineering evidence (EP-03 readiness review, existing code), not on roadmap intent. Caveat: R-89 is only PREPARED, so it is a conforming draft act with no force. It authorizes nothing yet, and no execution under it is recorded.

bearing.c1: AGAINST: one case, one episode (a single RED commit at a single boundary). It is enough to refute a universal claim that all recorded work conforms, but it says nothing about how often non-conformance happens. It is mitigated, not cured: the commit disclosed the outstanding Board acts, wrote no production code, and WP-4B was later accepted (R-87). Acceptance does not ratify the start.
bearing.c2: NEITHER: R-89 is a governance act, not recorded work, and it is PREPARED rather than in force. That it conforms to the gate shows the governance sequencing was respected in one episode. It is not evidence that work conforms to norms in force.
